items.action: Regular ferry crossing links Belém, Porto Brandão and Trafaria across the Tagus mouth, a short distance from the Atlantic; the trip takes about 30 minutes.
Belém river station, with simple architecture, black-and-white marble floor and wooden benches, was built in 1940 as a quay supporting the Exposição do Mundo Português.
Very few passengers travel to the south bank from Belém; the large ferry carries little cargo and sometimes no cars.
items.cargo: few people, little cargo, sometimes no cars

items.action: Historically the Tagus was the only road for national and intercontinental trade and linked the two banks; the crossing still carries this maritime heritage.
Intense river and maritime activity lasted until the 1970s; building the Ponte 25 de Abril abruptly changed this landscape.
On a morning crossing toward Lisbon, about twenty cars and people were seen travelling; the boats take something from the south bank but bring little back.
